title: Nearly one in three homes was rented
description: A hundred-square waffle shows Australia’s five tenure categories in 2021. Each square is approximately one per cent; the exact shares are listed below.

title: The separate house still defines the landscape
description: A treemap nests storey and building types inside five dwelling categories. Area represents occupied private dwellings. Tiny subtypes remain in the data table.

title: Apartments have a different tenure mix
description: Read this mosaic as columns: wider columns mean more homes of that dwelling type; the coloured heights show tenure within each type. Separate houses, townhouses, apartments, other, then not stated run left to right.

title: Who lives in which kind of home?
description: Bands connect household composition to dwelling type. Wider bands mean more households, not movement between homes. Other and unreported dwelling types are combined here.

title: A national median hides local differences
description: Colour shows each region’s median weekly rent, in $50 steps. Darker means higher rent; grey means no data. Outlines mark the three featured communities.

title: Where rented homes are concentrated
description: Circle area shows rented homes in 88 larger Census regions (SA4). Darker colour means a greater share renting. City insets use larger circles; read them with their own size key.

title: Most regional medians sit in the middle
description: Each bar counts regions whose median weekly rent falls within a $50 interval. This is a distribution of regional medians, not a distribution of renters or their rent payments.

title: Higher-income places often have higher rents
description: One dot is one region. Dashed lines show the published Australian household medians: $1,746 income and $375 rent per week. The association does not establish causation, and dividing these regional medians would not measure rental stress.

title: There is no single rental market within a state
description: Each row is one state. The line runs from its cheapest region to its dearest. The box holds the middle half of its regions. The white mark is the typical region. A long row means rents vary a lot.

title: Similar rents can come with very different homes
description: Each line is one region, read across four axes. Each axis has its own scale. Higher means more, not better. Monthly mortgages are shown weekly (×12÷52).

title: The cost of renting keeps changing
description: Both lines begin at 0% in April 2024. +10% means prices are 10% higher than then. These are eight-capital-city CPI measures, not advertised rents.

title: Some still spend over half their income on rent
description: Darker states have a larger share of assistance recipients paying over half their income in rent, after assistance. Small states are labelled offshore.

title: Payment groups face different levels of pressure
description: Each cell shows the percentage in rental stress after assistance within that state and primary payment group. The six selected groups are distinct published categories, not the entire recipient population. Student / apprentice means Youth Allowance; single parent means Parenting Payment (Single).

title: Assistance reduces the measured burden
description: Each pair describes the same recipients in March 2026. “Without” is a calculation that leaves assistance out, not an earlier observation or a controlled policy experiment. Rental stress means rent exceeds 30% of gross income.
